evidence: Inspected the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A6:D6 and Internal Quality Checks!A6:D6 both require that the prompt never name the judge, rubric, dimensions, weights, test paths or grader sentinels. Deterministic Checks!A14:C14 additionally identifies criterion IDs and long verbatim criterion overlap. Applied frozen Harbor quality-checks.md:25-27 and deterministic-checks.md:58,77-78, together with the staged contract's public instruction/private tests separation and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. All 84 frozen task/rules files matched their individual manifest SHA256 values; the manifest input_sha256 matches this report. Hereafter paths are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task unless otherwise stated. Read all seven participant-facing Markdown files completely: instruction.md and all six environment/instructions/*.md notes. Their contents describe product and deployment behavior, not grading machinery. For example instruction.md:5 says 'Please read the six notes in /instructions before you start'; integration.md:5 states 'We start it with node /app/server.js' and the public GET /api/health requirement; security.md:11 says 'Saving and loading snippets should store their source as text.' These are runtime/product facts, not private test paths or sentinels. environment/Dockerfile:14-15 copies only instructions/ and assets/ into their public locations, and environment/assets/seed_data.json contains only the product name, an empty snippets array and a product-scope note. Ran scripts/check_public_criterion_ids.py against the frozen task: 79 criteria across all five judge.toml files, seven public files, zero colliding IDs, passed true. Ran scripts/check_public_grader_terms.py: seven public files, zero matches, passed true. Independently ran the skill's broader judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score.py|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel search across all seven public Markdown files: zero matches (rg exit 1 denotes no matches, not a failed review). Read all 79 parsed criterion descriptions and compared their normalized consecutive words against each public file; the largest overlap was six words, 'copy of the last successful document', between behaviour.md:5 and cw_css_apply_snapshot. This is the necessary CSS product behavior, not lengthy copied grading text. Private fixture values remain private: tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25 requires a title starting with 'CW gate '; tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:171 assigns window.__cancelLeak; :270 uses forEeach; :285 calls undefinedFunctionCall. None occurs in any public Markdown. Also verified zero public occurrences of html-dispatch-ok, latest-good-B, async-error-marker, primitive-error-marker, auto-queued and failed-loop-candidate. Inspected the other four private prompt files and app_context.md to distinguish the private grading context from builder instructions. No actual grader-machinery leak was found. This is a static instruction-hygiene conclusion, not a hosted/private checker result or an Oracle, model-score or full-judge runtime claim.
counterexample: Exercised two in-memory adversarial prose witnesses without changing frozen source. A conforming alternative, 'Adjust the font weight so the editor stays readable.', matches the skill's broad regex on weight but exposes no scoring weight; manual semantic review must not fail it. A genuinely leaking alternative, 'Name saved examples starting with CW gate so they are recognized.', exposes the exact private title prefix from tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25 while producing zero broad-vocabulary hits, zero narrow-grader-marker hits and zero criterion-ID hits. This proves why passing the two local guards alone would be insufficient. The actual seven public files contain neither this private prefix nor any observed private marker, so these witnesses do not establish a defect in the frozen candidate. This row evaluates prompt exposure; app correctness alone cannot create or cure a prompt leak.
